small_guidance:
- Add larger-N tile configs (BLOCK_N=128, 256) to the autotune grid since OC=64 fits perfectly in a single BLOCK_N=64 tile but the M dimension is huge (M=128*14*62*62≈6.9M); try BLOCK_M=128/256 with BLOCK_N=64 and num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4.
- The K dimension is small (K=8*27=216); use BLOCK_K=64 or even unroll fully with BLOCK_K=128 plus a single masked iteration to eliminate loop overhead and let the compiler keep weights in registers.
- Swap the grid axis order (pid_n outer, pid_m inner) or use a swizzled tile order to improve L2 reuse of the small weight matrix across many M-tiles.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an output-stationary layout where each program owns a contiguous (OH, OW) tile (e.g. 8×8 or 16×16 spatial) for a single (n, oc-tile) pair and iterates over (ic, kt, kh, kw); this lets input rows be reused across kw and avoids the costly per-element decomposition of a flat M index. The 6.9M-element flat GEMM is wasting register pressure on index math.
- Cast as channels_last_3d (NDHWC) so the GEMM-K axis (IC*KT*KH*KW) has IC innermost-contiguous; current NCDHW layout makes IC strided by ID*IH*IW, hurting coalescing on x_tile loads.
- Consider a persistent-kernel design with one program per (n, oc_tile) sweeping the full OD*OH*OW space; with OC=64 and N=128 there are only ~128 programs needed if each handles all spatial outputs, giving better weight reuse (weight tile loaded once per program).
